root_cause.text: In the RDMA/rxe responder, check_rkey() failed to enforce the ATOMIC_WRITE protocol-mandated 8-byte payload length, allowing zero-length ATOMIC_WRITE packets to reach atomic_write_reply(), which unconditionally reads a u64 from payload_addr(pkt) past the logical packet end.
root_cause.evidence: The patch splits RXE_ATOMIC_WRITE_MASK from normal WRITE handling and adds `if (resid != sizeof(u64) || pktlen != sizeof(u64) || bth_pad(pkt))` to reject invalid ATOMIC_WRITE lengths; the commit message states `check_rkey() previously accepted an ATOMIC_WRITE request with pktlen == resid == 0` and that `atomic_write_reply()` unconditionally does `value = *(u64 *)payload_addr(pkt);`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Validate atomic write packets as exact 8-byte payloads with no padding to reject malformed requests and prevent out-of-bounds payload reads.
intent_record.what: The single write-length check was split into two branches: a new first branch handles packets with RXE_ATOMIC_WRITE_MASK and adds validation that resid and pktlen are exactly sizeof(u64) and that bth_pad(pkt) is zero, returning RESPST_ERR_LENGTH on failure; the existing write-path length check was moved into an else-if branch that now applies only to RXE_WRITE_MASK.
intent_record.how: At runtime, atomic write requests are now rejected unless their payload is exactly 8 bytes with no padding, preventing the responder from processing malformed atomic write packets and avoiding a potential read past the logical end of the packet payload.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows both the new ATOMIC_WRITE handling in `check_rkey()` and the new `atomic_write_reply()` implementation where the out-of-bounds read would occur. The vulnerable construct is present: `check_rkey()` was extended to treat `RXE_ATOMIC_WRITE_MASK` like writes (`if (pkt->mask & (RXE_READ_OR_WRITE_MASK | RXE_ATOMIC_WRITE_MASK))` and later `if (pkt->mask & (RXE_WRITE_MASK | RXE_ATOMIC_WRITE_MASK))`), but there is no special validation that an ATOMIC_WRITE payload must be exactly 8 bytes. In `atomic_write_reply()`, the code does `int payload = payload_size(pkt);` and then unconditionally consumes payload bytes into a 64-bit source with `memcpy(&src, payload_addr(pkt), payload);`. Because no 8-byte length check is enforced here or in `check_rkey()`, a zero-length ATOMIC_WRITE can reach this function. That matches the root cause: ATOMIC_WRITE protocol-mandated 8-byte payload length is not enforced before reply processing. The fix is not present, because there is no guard such as rejecting `payload != sizeof(u64)` / `payload != 8` for ATOMIC_WRITE packets before the `memcpy` and atomic store logic.

The root cause is that ATOMIC_WRITE/atomic requests must enforce an 8-byte payload length before later atomic processing reads the payload. In `check_rkey()`, atomic packets are handled by `else if (pkt->mask & RXE_ATOMIC_MASK) { qp->resp.va = atmeth_va(pkt); qp->resp.rkey = atmeth_rkey(pkt); qp->resp.resid = sizeof(u64); access = IB_ACCESS_REMOTE_ATOMIC; }`, but there is no validation that `payload_size(pkt)` equals 8 for atomic operations. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present: atomic packets are accepted without the protocol-mandated 8-byte payload-length enforcement. No fix is present in this version because there is no atomic-specific `pktlen == sizeof(u64)` or equivalent check in `check_rkey()`/`check_length()` before execution.
